gpp.note: The one action colour. Same value as lucuma-ui --green-500 (#4caf50); prefer the lucuma-ui variable where it is in scope.

gpp-light.note: Hover fill, and the focus step: 3.35:1 on the active-nav fill where the base green is 2.91:1.

gpp-accent.note: Identity only. Never interactive, never a state.

canvas.note: Step 0 of the chrome ladder measured from Explore. The ramp is the whole ladder, canvas to subtle; climb it in order and never invent an intermediate grey.

surface-raised.note: Table headers, and the one hover step for every surface.

foreground.note: A white-opacity ladder (Material dark), not a grey ramp.

foreground-secondary.note: The floor tone for information at every size.

foreground-muted.note: Fails AA on every surface in the ladder at any size, so it may never be the only carrier of information.

warning.note: The ramp is the panel triplet plus the canvas weight: fill, edge, word, ink.

danger.note: The ramp is the panel triplet plus the canvas weight: fill, edge, word, ink.

schedule-closed.note: Telescope shutdown on the charts, solid. Declared as --schedule-closed, not --color-closure-red.

state-routine.note: Schedule state rows are monochrome on purpose: hue means instrument identity and nothing else.

instrument-unknown.note: A reserved neutral outside the two validated site hue sets; it must read as "identity unresolved".

title.purpose: One page title per destination, in PageHeader. Exactly one element on a page may carry it.

body.purpose: Anything a reader reads as words: cells, controls, prose, messages, empty states. The default, set once on body.

dense.purpose: The chrome and every dense data surface. The floor for informative text; the weight (400-700) is the call site’s.

tick.purpose: Numeric axis tick labels and nothing else. Below the informative floor, which is why nothing informative may take it.

wordmark.purpose: "RESOURCE" is not a size: it sits at Body and takes its identity from 700 weight and 0.4em tracking.

extensions.shadowPolicy: None. The system is flat and tonal: depth is stated by climbing the surface ladder, never by box-shadow. The two exceptions are the modal scrim and the chart tooltip’s 1px border, both under unmappedTokens.

breakpoints.name: md
breakpoints.purpose: The shell’s one breakpoint, written 48rem in shell.css and md: in Tailwind. Below it the phone frame replaces the sidebar with a bottom bar; at and above it the desktop shell is untouched.

breakpoints.name: sm
breakpoints.purpose: A verification width, not a design width: 640 CSS px is 200% zoom on a 1280px screen (WCAG 1.4.4), so max-sm: reads natively as "below the AA zoom point".

breakpoints.name: reflow
breakpoints.purpose: A verification width, not a design width: WCAG 1.4.10 reflow. A chart or a data table may scroll inside its own container; nothing else may be lost or put out of reach.

treatments.name: FOCUS_RING
treatments.appliesTo: the app’s own elements (masthead, phone bar today)
treatments.css: outline: none; box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 2px var(--color-gpp-light, hsl(122deg 39% 55%));

treatments.name: segmented control outline
treatments.why: An outline rather than a ring: the selected segment spends its box-shadow on the underline, so a focus shadow would be replaced by it and the segment a keyboard lands on first would show no focus at all.

focusRing.contrast: The light green step, not the base one. The base green measures 2.91:1 against the translucent green an active nav item fills with, under WCAG 1.4.11’s 3:1 floor for a UI part; the light step measures 3.35:1.
focusRing.shortfalls: Week cards ride the browser-default ring, and chart bars are mouse-only with no keyboard path to a bar’s open-night action.

unmappedTokens.name: --schedule-band
unmappedTokens.purpose: The one translucent closure wash laid over the subject rows. A shutdown is said once, per chart, never per row.

unmappedTokens.name: --instrument-ink-light
unmappedTokens.purpose: Bar label ink where light clears 4.5:1 on the instrument fill.

unmappedTokens.name: --instrument-ink-dark
unmappedTokens.purpose: Bar label ink where dark clears 4.5:1 on the instrument fill.

unmappedTokens.name: --timeline-block-border
unmappedTokens.purpose: A 1px separator between adjacent blocks that share a hue.

unmappedTokens.name: modal scrim
unmappedTokens.purpose: One of the two exceptions to the flat rule: the darker scrim (60% against the theme’s 40%) plus the blur together state that a modal is up.

unmappedTokens.name: chart tooltip radius
unmappedTokens.purpose: features/timeline/timelineOptions.ts. Larger than the 4px control radius because a tooltip is an overlay, not a control.

unmappedTokens.name: schedule bar radius
unmappedTokens.purpose: Softens a corner without moving an edge off its time. A bar’s edges are facts (half-open intervals), so no rounding or padding may move one.

extensions.tokenSource: src/styles/global.css (@theme and the chart variables) and src/styles/shell.css are normative for every value. DESIGN.md is normative for every rule. Neither this file nor DESIGN.md’s frontmatter is a complete token list: the fourteen-hue instrument palette, both block inks, the --timeline-* variables, the washes and the grid lines live only in the CSS.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one action colour. At most one primary action per view, and today’s read-only views correctly have none.

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Slate fill for a control that must not read as the primary action.

components.name: Icon Button
components.description: 28px square, transparent at rest. Hover climbs one step of the surface ladder; disabled drops to 40%. Always carries an accessible name.
components.css: .ds-icon-btn { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 28px; height: 28px; background: transparent; border: none; color: var(--color-foreground-secondary, rgb(255 255 255 / 60%)); border-radius: 4px; cursor: pointer; } .ds-icon-btn:not(:disabled):hover { background: var(--color-surface-raised, #414141); color: var(--color-foreground, rgb(255 255 255 / 87%)); } .ds-icon-btn:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 2px var(--color-gpp-light, hsl(122deg 39% 55%)); } .ds-icon-btn:disabled { opacity: 0.4; cursor: default; }

components.name: Status Tag

components.html: Science Engineering Spare Unavailable

narrative.overview:
Resource is one console among the GPP applications, and it must feel like it: a reader coming from Explore (https://explore-dev.lucuma.xyz/) stays in the same dark, dense, matter-of-fact world. The chrome was measured from the running Explore application - the surface ladder, the white-opacity text ladder, the action green, the lightgreen identity accent - and those measured values are recorded here as tokens. Continuity is a floor, not a ceiling: where Resource can achieve clearer hierarchy, stronger accessibility, better interaction design, or more efficient use of space than Explore, it does, without breaking the family resemblance.

The surface is an information-dense engineering dashboard for experts - astronomers, night operations, staff - who scan, compare, and monitor the same views repeatedly. Density wins ties: condensed is correct here, airy is not. The interface recedes behind the record; colour is spent on identity and alarm, never on decoration. Today every view reads; mutations, auth, and a telescope scheduler builder are coming, so every pattern below is chosen to survive the arrival of editing (see Future Readiness).
keyCharacteristics: Dark-first and only: black canvas, tonal layering, no glare, minimal chrome.
Dense: type and the boxes that hold it in rem so a reader can scale them, spacing in px so it does not.
Colour is semantic: hue = instrument identity, red = telescope closure, green = action.
Honest: a gap draws as a gap; absence is hollow; unknown is grey. Nothing is decorated to look complete (invariant I4 in PRODUCT.md).
WCAG 2.2 Level AA is the target, not an aspiration.

rules.name: The One Green Rule
rules.body: Action green acts; light-green accent identifies; no third green exists. If a green element does nothing when pressed, it must be the accent; if it acts, it must be `--color-gpp`.

rules.name: Red Is the Telescope's Alone (on the charts)
rules.body: A shutdown is said once: a solid red block on the Telescope row, one translucent band wash over the subject rows, the reason printed once on the band, one legend key. Never per-row red painting - the ports are not each closed, and no other row may claim red. Off the charts, red says only closed, unavailable, or error.

rules.name: Hue Means Identity and Nothing Else
rules.body: Chart hue identifies an instrument. States are monochrome; do not give a state a hue - a new state kind joins the two neutrals or the closure red. Identity never rides on colour alone: every block, row and swatch carries its published name in words.

rules.name: Treatment, Not a Second Palette
rules.body: Usability is a treatment over the identity hue: Science is the plain bar; Engineering-use the same hue hatched; Not-available hollow with the hue on the outline and a muted label - visually distinct from the ghost, and never red. Absence is drawn hollow (`schedule-ghost`), never as another identity colour, and never red either.

rules.name: A Gap Is a Gap
rules.body: Empty cells, empty calendar squares, and unrecorded spans stay empty. "Not recorded" must never be styled as "closed" or "unavailable" (invariant I4).

rules.name: The One-Number Rule
rules.body: Density is one number: `--spacing` in `@theme`, **3.5px**. Every Tailwind spacing utility compiles to `calc(var(--spacing) * n)`, so that one value sets every gap, padding and margin written as a utility. Never fix a layout problem by nudging it. **The number is not a single switch, though.** `shell.css` and `global.css` also carry multiples of the step derived by hand and written as literals - 12.6, 9.8, 8.4, 7.7, 4.2, 3.5, 2.8 and 2.1px - and those do not move when `--spacing` does. Changing the step means re-deriving every px figure in those two stylesheets in the same commit; half-done, the app silently runs at two densities, which the Don't list forbids.

rules.name: The app sets no root font size
rules.body: , which is what lets a reader's own browser font-size setting scale the type. Comeau's question decides which unit a value takes: _should this grow when the reader raises that setting?_ Type says yes, and so does any box whose job is to hold type - a width or a height that has to grow with the words inside it, the chart's label gutter being the worked example. Spacing says no and is written in px: gaps, padding, margins, border widths, and the target tokens (`--xp-target-floor`, `--xp-touch-target`), because a finger is a finger. An absolute px root would pin all of it and silently disable the setting.

rules.name: Dense Is The Floor
rules.body: No role carrying information sits below 12px. Tick is the single named exception and it is not information: a tick number repeats what its axis already says. Secondary (60%) is the floor tone for information at every size; muted carries only decoration or duplication (the same rule the Colors ladder states).

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: No new shadow vocabulary. If a surface needs to read as above another, move it up the ladder.

rules.name: The One-Library Rule
rules.body: Every component is PrimeReact's: buttons, dialogs, menus, tables, inputs and overlays come from `primereact/*` and take the lucuma-ui theme, always. A hand-written element that imitates a component PrimeReact ships is not an option; plain HTML with Tailwind is for what PrimeReact has no component for - a caption, a live region, a line of text - never for a look-alike control.

rules.name: The One-Glyph-Set Rule
rules.body: Every icon or glyph is a FontAwesome icon rendered through `FontAwesomeIcon`, sized by FontAwesome's own `size` prop: no image logos, no inline SVG, no PrimeIcons. Brand marks (ORCID) come from FontAwesome's brands set and take the theme's ink like any other glyph.

dos: **Do** climb the surface ladder in order; a new layer takes the next step, not a new hex.
**Do** spend colour on data. Chrome stays neutral so instruments and alarms own the hue.
**Do** put every control on the 28px line and every caption through `LabelledControl`.
**Do** show the published name (`'Alopeke`, Maroon-X), never the enum, and keep the name in words beside every colour.
**Do** give every chart a block-table reading - the semester chart's screen-reader table is the model, and the night and week charts still owe theirs - and drive tests through accessible queries.
**Do** target WCAG 2.2 AA on every change: 4.5:1 text, 3:1 UI parts, visible focus, 24px minimum targets (or spacing equivalents), full keyboard paths.
**Do** design every new component with its editing states in mind (see Future Readiness), even while the app is read-only.
donts: **Don't** hard-code a colour in a component - extend from the tokens; components read variables.
**Don't** give a schedule state a hue, a port its own red, or absence a colour.
**Don't** decorate a gap. No skeleton rows, placeholder bars, or "probably fine" fills where the record holds nothing.
**Don't** use the identity accent (`--color-gpp-accent`) on anything interactive.
**Don't** put informative text below 60% white, or below Dense (12px), anywhere new (the shipped deviations are catalogued by pattern under Typography and queued to be fixed).
**Don't** add a masthead item without re-measuring the width budget.
**Don't** introduce a second density: no per-view font-size overrides to make something fit; fix the layout instead.
**Don't** set a root font size on `html`. An absolute one disables the reader's own browser font-size setting; density belongs to `--spacing` and to the px chrome values.
**Don't** copy an Explore weakness for continuity's sake - continuity binds palette, density and family resemblance, not defects.
